devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

occurrences.note: " The villages ceased ": i.e., the inhabitants of the villages, or the Peasantry. So also v. 11
The breaking of bonds (of various kinds) is put for liberating from servitude
"And bound him with two brasses": i.e., two brazen fetters

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: "And Samson said. Let my soul (i.e., me, as in A.V., see margin) die with the Philistines."
" I shall give thee ten shekels of silver for the days ": i.e., by the year, as in A.V

devices.name: Enigma
devices.definition: A dark saying — a truth wrapped in obscure or riddling terms.

occurrences.note: Samson's Enigma is well known. " Out of the eater came forth meat, And out of the strong came forth sweetness."

devices.name: Ellipsis
devices.definition: A word or words deliberately left out, to be supplied by the reader — compression and force.

occurrences.note: Here, because the Ellipsis has not been observed, liberties have been taken in the translation. The Heb. is literally " In the days of Jael the highways ceased " (as in verse 7). The A.V. and R.V
margin, "a woman an harlot."

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

occurrences.note: meant merely vigorous; and Lust meant simply pleasure or desire generally

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

occurrences.note: " He (i.e., Israel) will choose (i.e., he chose) new Gods." For Deborah is speaking of the cause of the affliction which had fallen upon the People: viz., idolatry
" O my soul, thou wilt tread down strength ": i.e., tread thou down (not, as in A.V., " hast trodden down "); or, R.V.: " march on."

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

occurrences.note: " Every one could sling stones at an hair and not miss": to describe the wonderful proficiency which the Benjamites had attained in slinging stones. The A.V. has added breadth in italics, so as to

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

occurrences.note: " Then Jephthah fled from his brethren." Here the A.V. has again omitted the word " face," but in this case has put it in the margin

devices.name: Synonymia
devices.definition: Amassing synonyms — words of like meaning — to enforce and enlarge a point.

occurrences.note: also of the feet, to miss the step or footing; and hence, stumble; then, to err, go astray, trespass. Every departure from God is, therefore, a missing of the mark, and trespass against Him. (3)

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

occurrences.note: " His soul was grieved for the misery of Israel."

devices.name: Aposiopesis
devices.definition: A sentence broken off unfinished, as if the speaker cannot or will not go on.

devices.name: Personification
devices.definition: Giving human traits, action, or speech to something impersonal or abstract.

devices.name: Allegory
devices.definition: An extended metaphor — a whole passage whose surface story stands throughout for a deeper meaning.

devices.name: Anacoluthon
devices.definition: A break in grammatical sequence — a sentence begun one way and finished another.

devices.name: Anaphora
devices.definition: The same word or phrase begins a run of successive clauses, hammering a theme.

occurrences.note: " At her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay down: At her feet he bowed, he fell: where he bowed, there he fell down dead."

devices.name: Anteisagoge
devices.definition: Meeting a question or objection with a counter-question.

devices.name: Antonomasia
devices.definition: A proper name replaced by a descriptive title, or a title by a proper name (“the Son of man”).

occurrences.note: So also other appellatives are used: e.g., " The Seed of the woman," " The Messiah," " The Servant of Jehovah," " The Messenger of the Covenant," " The Prophet,"

devices.name: Asyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions omitted between items in a series, producing a rapid, piled-up effect.

occurrences.note: "At her feet he bowed, —he fell, — he lay down; — at her feet he bowed, —he fell: — where he bowed, there he fell down dead."

devices.name: Epiphonema
devices.definition: A closing exclamation that sums up and drives home what has just been said.

occurrences.note: " So let all thine enemies perish, O Lord."

devices.name: Epitheton
devices.definition: Naming a thing by an attribute or adjunct added to it (“John the Baptist”).

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for intense emphasis, with nothing between (“Lord, Lord”).

devices.name: Euphemism
devices.definition: A softened or decent expression put for one that is harsh or delicate (“fallen asleep”).

occurrences.note: " Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber." When an Eastern stoops down, his garments fall over and cover his feet. Hence the Euphemy, the meaning of which is given in the margin

devices.name: Hendiadys
devices.definition: One idea expressed by two words joined with “and,” the second really qualifying the first.

devices.name: Hyperbaton
devices.definition: Words wrenched out of their natural order, throwing weight onto the displaced word.

devices.name: Irony
devices.definition: Saying the opposite of what is meant, so the real sense is felt through the contrast.

occurrences.note: "Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your tribulation." This was Divine Sarcasm, for those gods could neither hear nor deliver

devices.name: Metaphor
devices.definition: An implied comparison that calls one thing another (“A is B”), without “like” or “as.”

occurrences.note: will give peace. In verse 3. " He restoreth my soul," for Hi is Jehovah

devices.name: Parable
devices.definition: A continued simile — a narrative laid alongside a truth to teach it by comparison.

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Successive lines echo one another in structure — saying the same thing twice, or balancing matched clauses.

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

devices.name: Periphrasis
devices.definition: Circumlocution: a description put in place of the plain name of a thing.

devices.name: Polysyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions (“and … and …”) piled up to slow the pace and weight every item.

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.
